title: Coco Ichibanya Owner Considering Sale
paragraphs: CoCo Ichibanya, Japan's most popular curry rice restaurant chain, may soon have a new owner.

On August 31, House Foods Group, a major Japanese food company, confirmed a newspaper report that it is considering selling its stake in Ichibanya, the company that runs the chain. House Foods owns 51% of the company. However, House Foods said that no decision has been made. Both companies said that all options are being considered, including taking Ichibanya private.
After the news came out, Ichibanya's shares jumped by 16%.

CoCo Ichibanya was started in Nagoya in 1978. From the beginning, it used curry sauce made by House Foods. Over the years, House Foods slowly bought more and more of Ichibanya's shares. In 2015, it paid 30 billion yen to raise its share from 19.5% to 51%.
According to reports, House Foods is reviewing all of its businesses and wants to focus on the ones that are most profitable and have the best chance of growing.

The curry chain has been facing some problems. The cost of ingredients has gone up, but it is difficult to raise prices too much because curry is seen as a cheap comfort food. Many people in Japan also cook curry at home. Since 2024, the chain has lost some customers after raising its prices.
In the business year that ended in February 2026, Ichibanya's sales rose by 7.4% to 65.5 billion yen. However, its profit fell by 19.2% to 2.5 billion yen, mainly because of higher ingredient costs.

According to Bloomberg, Ichibanya is likely to attract interest from large buyers, including investment companies. For now, however, it is not clear who might buy the business, or whether a sale will happen at all. Many fans in Japan are watching the news closely.
